page.text:
A *vector space* (or linear space) over a field $F$ is an algebraic
universe governed by the principle of *superposition*: elements (vectors)
can be added together and scaled by scalars from $F$.

Axiomatically, vector addition $(V, +, 0)$ constitutes an abelian group,
providing translation, subtraction, and a zero vector. Scalar
multiplication $\cdot : F \times V \to V$ acts as a field action
compatible with addition: it distributes across both vector addition and
field addition, associates with field multiplication, and acts unitally
with $1 \in F$.

From geometric displacement arrows in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and coordinate
spaces $F^n$, to function spaces $C^k(\mathbb{R})$, polynomial rings
$F[x]$, and quantum Hilbert spaces, vector spaces provide the uniform
structural medium for all linear phenomena.
